recommendation_summary: The reply recommends wrapping the cron call to nightly-sync in a shell script with a trap that emails the user on any nonzero exit, with no new service, Synology or Docker.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to know when nightly-sync fails, not to see logs. "Central log on Synology" and "Docker" are your proposed means.
labels.Deleted: A centralized logging stack (Loki/ELK/etc. in Docker on the Synology). You'd be running and maintaining a log platform to solve a problem that's really "I never got an alert."
labels.Bottleneck: nightly-sync dies before it reaches its own email step, so the one notification path you have never fires on failure.
labels.Checked myself: You told me cron runs it at 03:00 on edna, it crashed at startup (expired token) four nights straight, and the email only happens on successful completion.

note: The self-hosted healthchecks container is deferred conditionally rather than recommended now; the phrase 'any nonzero exit, success or failure' contradicts itself but does not change the class.
